info.title: Ovation Partner API Documentation
info.description:
# Overview

Welcome to the **Ovation Partner API** documentation. This guide will help you understand how to interact with our services, including authentication, endpoints, and best practices.

## Authentication

Our API uses OAuth2 for authentication. To access protected endpoints, you need to obtain an access token using our `/oauth2/access-token` endpoint. When making this request, you must include your `client_id` and `client_secret` in the `Authorization` header as `Basic client_id:client_secret` (base64 encoded), and set the `X-Ovation-Id` header to identify the partner name.

The access token you receive will be valid for 1 hour. After this period, you will need to request a new token using the same authentication process.

Once you have the token, you can include it in the `Authorization` header of your requests when interacting with other endpoints.

### Headers Required:

1. **When Getting an Access Token**:
   - `Authorization`: `Basic clientId:secret` (base64 encoded)
   - `X-Ovation-Id`: Partner name (required)

2. **When Making Other Requests**:
   - `Authorization`: `Bearer your-access-token`
   - `X-Ovation-Id`: Partner name (required)
   - `X-Api-Key`: The `api_key` received from the access token response (required)

### Base URLs
- **Sandbox**: `https://partner-staging.ovationup.com/partner-services/v2`
- **Production**: `https://partner.ovationup.com/partner-services/v2`

### Example of Using Access Token:
```http
Authorization: Bearer your-access-token
X-Ovation-Id: your-partner-name
X-Api-Key: your-api-key
```

## Quick Start

1. **Get Access Token**: Use your `client_id` and `client_secret` to request an access token.
2. **Make API Requests**: Include the token in your `Authorization` header and set `X-Ovation-Id` and `X-Api-Key` headers.
3. **Explore Endpoints**: Refer to the specific endpoint documentation below for details on request and response structures.

## Error Handling

Errors are communicated using standard HTTP status codes:

- `400`: Bad Request â€“ The request was invalid.
- `401`: Unauthorized â€“ Authentication failed.
- `403`: Forbidden â€“ You do not have access to the requested resource.
- `404`: Not Found â€“ The requested resource could not be found.
- `409`: Conflict â€“ The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource.
- `500`: Internal Server Error â€“ A server error occurred.

post.description:
Retrieves the timeline of events related to a specific conversation, with support for pagination and filtering.

**Pagination Behavior:**
- `previous_limit` is **only used when** `starting_event_id` is provided.
- `next_limit` can be used **whenever needed**, regardless of `starting_event_id`.

**Scenarios:**
1. **Load most recent 50 events:** Set `next_limit: 50` and omit `starting_event_id`.
2. **Scroll to previous events:** Set `previous_limit: 50`, `next_limit: 0`, `starting_event_id: events[0]._id`.
3. **Load timeline at a specific event (e.g., search result):** Set `previous_limit: 25`, `next_limit: 25`, `starting_event_id: found_event._id`.

next_limit.description: Number of events to fetch after `starting_event_id`. **Can be used at any time**.

types.description: A list of event types to filter by.

starting_event_id.description: The ID of the analytic event from which to start the timeline. Required for `previous_limit` to work.
